name: r520_init
prose: Returns int (r520.c:250-329). It initialises the scratch registers and surfaces and restores sanity. It returns -EINVAL if no BIOS can be obtained on an AVIVO ASIC, and returns -EINVAL if the BIOS is not an ATOM BIOS (with a message naming RV515); an error from radeon_atombios_init is returned. It then tries an ASIC reset (only warning on failure), returns -EINVAL if the card fails the post test, posts the card through atom_asic_init when it is not posted and a BIOS exists, reads the clock info, initialises AGP (disabling it on failure), the memory controller, debugfs, the fence driver, the buffer object manager (error returned) and the PCIE GART (error returned), sets the safe register table and initialises power management. It sets accel_working to true and calls r520_startup; if that fails it logs, tears down the CP, writeback, IB pool, IRQs, GART and AGP and sets accel_working to false, but the function still returns 0. Otherwise it returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: the packet slice lies inside r520_init (head at r520.c:250); rv515_init is in a different file. The behaviour that startup failure is not returned (the function returns 0 with acceleration disabled) is at 316-328. R:n/a

name: r600_packet3_check
prose: Static int (r600_cs.c:1631-2275) that validates one type-3 packet of an R600 command stream with a switch on the opcode. For each supported opcode it checks the packet count and fields (register windows for SET_* packets, buffer and offset sizes, texture and vertex resources), fetches relocations with radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc where an address is present and patches the IB words with the relocated GPU offset and tiling bits, updates the tracker, and runs r600_cs_track_check for draw packets. It returns 0 for a valid packet (including packets with a clear operation that return early, and NOP) and -EINVAL for a wrong count, a failed field check, a buffer that is too small, a missing relocation (radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc failures are converted to -EINVAL after a message) or an unsupported opcode; the results of r600_cs_check_reg, r600_check_texture_resource and r600_cs_track_check are returned unchanged.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at r600_cs.c:1631). Reviewer claim (relocation failures return -EINVAL, not the error of radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc) is right. The function has about 645 lines, so the prose is deliberately general. R:right

name: r600_dma_cs_parse
prose: Returns int (r600_cs.c:2385-2534) and validates and relocates a whole DMA indirect buffer in a loop. At the start of every iteration it returns -EINVAL if p->idx is not below the chunk length. It decodes the command, count and tiled flag from the header and switches on the command. WRITE gets one destination relocation (tiled or linear form patch the offset words and advance p->idx by count plus 5 or 3, then the written range is checked against the destination object); COPY gets source and destination relocations and handles tiled and linear forms (RV770 and later or earlier layouts) with range checks against both objects; CONSTANT_FILL returns -EINVAL for families older than RV770, otherwise takes a destination relocation, checks the range and patches the words; NOP advances by one; any other command returns -EINVAL. A failed r600_dma_cs_next_reloc returns -EINVAL before p->idx is advanced; in the WRITE and COPY cases p->idx has already been advanced when the size check fails. The loop ends with return 0 when p->idx reaches the chunk length.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at r600_cs.c:2385). Reviewer claim (p->idx is not advanced on a relocation failure in WRITE and COPY, contrary to the old annotation) is right (2409-2413, 2435-2444). R:right

name: radeon_get_atom_connector_info_from_object_table
prose: Returns bool (radeon_atombios.c:517-831). It parses the Object_Header data header and returns false if that fails or the content revision is below 2. Otherwise it walks the display path table; for each path whose device tag is supported by the header and is not the CV device, it works out the connector type and object id (for an IGP PCIE connector from the IntegratedSystemInfo table's slot config when its revision is at least 2, otherwise from the connector object id; paths whose IGP lookup fails are skipped) and skips paths whose connector type is unknown. For each graphics object in the path it registers encoders with radeon_add_atom_encoder (with their capability record) and gathers router information (I2C, DDC and clock/data mux records); for non-TV, non-CV paths it finds the connector object and reads its I2C (DDC) and HPD records. It applies board quirks with radeon_atom_apply_quirks (a path rejected by the quirks is skipped) and registers each connector with radeon_add_atom_connector. After the loop it calls radeon_link_encoder_connector and returns true. It takes no locks and the caller releases nothing.
note: slice cut the head: the function is radeon_get_atom_connector_info_from_object_table's real name radeon_get_atom_connector_info_from_object_table (head at radeon_atombios.c:517; the packet name radeon_atombios_get_connector_info_from_object_table does not exist). Old prose omitted that encoders are registered here too and that paths can be skipped. R:n/a

name: radeon_gpu_reset
prose: Returns int (radeon_device.c:1755-1857). It takes rdev->exclusive_lock for writing; if rdev->needs_reset is false it releases it with up_write and returns 0. Otherwise it bumps gpu_reset_counter, saves the BIOS scratch registers, suspends the device, stops HPD, backs up each ring's pending commands, and calls radeon_asic_reset; on success it resumes the device. It restores the BIOS scratch registers, then for each ring either restores the saved commands (reset succeeded and data saved) or force-completes the ring's fences and frees the backup. It then redoes power management: radeon_pm_late_init when DPM is the method and enabled (its result replaces r, so a failed ASIC reset can be overwritten by a 0 result; a failed late init disables DPM) or radeon_pm_resume otherwise. For ATOM BIOS it reinitialises the encoders, the display engine PLL and the backlight, re-initialises HPD, sets in_reset and clears needs_reset, downgrades the lock to read mode, forces the display mode back, recomputes clocks for DPM, and, if r is 0 after those steps, runs radeon_ib_ring_tests (a failure with saved commands becomes -EAGAIN) or logs the failed reset. It sets needs_reset when r is -EAGAIN, clears in_reset, releases the read lock and returns r.
note: Checked against radeon_device.c:1755-1857. Reviewer claims: the early return uses up_write, not a read downgrade (right, 1766-1768); r can be overwritten by radeon_pm_late_init so a failed ASIC reset can end up returning 0 (right, 1807). R:right

name: radeon_fence_default_wait
prose: Static signed long (radeon_fence.c:1003-1043). It first calls dma_fence_add_callback; if that returns nonzero (for example the fence is already signalled) it returns t unchanged, without changing the task state. Otherwise, while t > 0 it sets the task state to interruptible or uninterruptible according to intr, breaks if the fence is signalled (t then keeps the value it had) or if rdev->needs_reset is set (t becomes -EDEADLK), else sleeps with schedule_timeout(t), and sets t to -ERESTARTSYS if the sleep ended with time left, intr is set and a signal is pending. After the loop it sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING, removes the callback and returns t: the remaining timeout, 0 on expiry, -EDEADLK or -ERESTARTSYS, or the original t if it was not positive.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at radeon_fence.c:1003). Reviewer claim (round 15: on a failed dma_fence_add_callback it can return -ERESTARTSYS) is wrong: that path returns t at line 1013 before any signal test. R:wrong

name: radeon_info_ioctl
prose: Returns int (radeon_kms.c:231-616) and implements the radeon info query ioctl with a switch on info->request, copying a value of the request's size to the user buffer at info->value. It returns -EFAULT when copy_from_user or copy_to_user fails, and -EINVAL for an unknown or unsupported request, an out-of-range input (WANT_HYPERZ and WANT_CMASK values of 2 or more, an unknown CRTC id or ring id, a disallowed register) or a request the device family does not support. For WANT_HYPERZ and WANT_CMASK the file's ownership flag is updated and the resulting ownership is reported. It returns 0 after the final copy_to_user succeeds. A failing copy_to_user can leave the user buffer partially written, so the buffer is not guaranteed unwritten on error.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at radeon_kms.c:231). Reviewer claim (a copy_to_user failure can leave the buffer partly written) is right. The function is about 386 lines, so the prose is deliberately general. R:right

name: uvd_v1_0_ib_test
prose: Returns int (uvd_v1_0.c:500-542). It raises the UVD clocks (10000/10000 for families older than RV740, 53300/40000 otherwise) and returns the error at once if that fails, without releasing anything. It then gets the UVD create message and the destroy message (with a fence); a failure of either goes to error. It waits for the fence for RADEON_USEC_IB_TEST_TIMEOUT microseconds: a negative result is returned, zero (timeout) becomes -ETIMEDOUT, and a positive result is a success, logged as such with result 0. At the error label, reached on every path after the clocks were raised including success, it releases the fence reference and sets the UVD clocks back to 0, then returns the result.
note: slice cut the head: the function is uvd_v1_0_ib_test (head at uvd_v1_0.c:500). The old prose described the fence release and clock reset only for failures; they also run on success. R:n/a

name: awg_generate_instr
prose: Static int (sti_awg_utils.c:28-118) that appends AWG RAM instruction words to fwparams. It loops while arg_tmp (initially arg) is positive; each iteration returns -EINVAL if fwparams->instruction_offset is already AWG_MAX_INST (words written by earlier iterations stay in ram_code and instruction_offset stays advanced) and then handles the opcode: SKIP decrements arg and arg_tmp and turns into SET when arg reaches 0, or clears mux and data enable and masks the argument; REPEAT and REPLAY clear mux and data enable and mask the argument; JUMP sets bit 6 of the argument and masks it; STOP sets arg to 0; SET, RPTSET, RPLSET and HOLD mask the argument to 8 bits; any other opcode returns -EINVAL. It subtracts the consumed arg from arg_tmp, combines arg, mux and data enable, stores the opcode and argument in 14 bits at ram_code[instruction_offset] and increments instruction_offset. Because arg is positive inside the loop, the SKIP arg < 0 return and the REPEAT/REPLAY arg == 0 return are never reached, so each iteration writes exactly one word. With arg <= 0 on entry nothing is written and it returns 0; otherwise it returns 0 when the loop ends.
note: Checked against sti_awg_utils.c:28-118. Reviewer claims: -EINVAL on the AWG_MAX_INST check can leave earlier words written (right, 48-51); the SKIP/REPEAT/REPLAY early returns are unreachable inside a loop that needs arg_tmp > 0 (right, 57-63, 79-82); round 15 claim (one word per iteration is false because those branches return 0 without writing) is wrong for the same reason. R:mixed

name: sti_crtc_vblank_cb
prose: Returns int (sti_crtc.c:242-279). It is a VTG vblank notifier callback: data is the drm_crtc, its index selects the pipe, and nb is the vtg_vblank_nb[pipe] member of the compositor from which the mixer is found. It returns -EINVAL (after logging) if event is neither VTG_TOP_FIELD_EVENT nor VTG_BOTTOM_FIELD_EVENT. Otherwise it calls drm_crtc_handle_vblank(crtc); if the mixer status is STI_MIXER_DISABLING it scans the device's planes and returns 0 at once if any GDP or VDP plane (type up to STI_VDP) is not STI_PLANE_DISABLED, otherwise it calls sti_crtc_disable(crtc). It returns 0 in all other cases.
note: slice cut the head: the function is sti_crtc_vblank_cb (head at sti_crtc.c:242), not sti_crtc_vblank; nb is the compositor's per-pipe notifier block and data carries the crtc, not a sti_crtc embedding nb. R:n/a

name: sun8i_vi_layer_init_one
prose: Returns struct sun8i_layer * or an ERR_PTR (sun8i_vi_layer.c:473-552). It allocates the layer itself with devm_kzalloc (ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) on failure), picks the DE3 or earlier format list, makes the plane the primary plane when the mixer has no UI layers and index is 0 (otherwise an overlay), and initialises it with drm_universal_plane_init (error returned as ERR_PTR). It creates the alpha property when the mixer has exactly one VI layer or is a DE3 or later mixer, the zpos property (range 0 to ui_num + vi_num - 1, default index) and the colour encoding and range properties (BT601 and BT709, plus BT2020 on DE3 or later; limited and full range; defaults BT709 and limited), each failure returning its error as an ERR_PTR. It adds the helper functions, sets layer->mixer, type SUN8I_LAYER_TYPE_VI, channel index and overlay 0, and returns the layer. The allocation is device managed, so error returns do not free it.

name: drm_dp_aux_detach
prose: Returns int (tegra/dpaux.c:757-793). It unregisters the AUX channel with drm_dp_aux_unregister and disables the AUX interrupt first. If the output has a panel it disables the VDD regulator when one exists (a negative result is returned, with dpaux->output still set), then polls drm_dp_aux_detect for up to 250 ms until the sink reports disconnected, sleeping 1-2 ms between polls, and returns -ETIMEDOUT with dpaux->output still set if it never does; on success it sets dpaux->output to NULL. It returns 0 in that case and when the output has no panel (in which case dpaux->output is left as it was).

name: ttm_bo_validate_happy_evict
prose: KUnit test (static void, ttm_bo_validate_test.c:761-815). It registers mock managers for TTM_PL_VRAM and TTM_PL_TT (both MANAGER_SIZE), creates three buffer objects of 8 KiB, 512 KiB and the remaining space in the VRAM manager, validates a further BO_SIZE buffer into VRAM, and checks with KUnit expectations that validation returned 0, that the first buffer object was evicted to TTM_PL_SYSTEM with TTM_TT_FLAG_ZERO_ALLOC and TTM_TT_FLAG_PRIV_POPULATED set, that bytes_moved equals 2 * 8 KiB + BO_SIZE and that the second buffer object is still in VRAM. It then puts all four buffer objects and finalises both mock managers. It returns nothing.

name: ttm_global_init
prose: Static int (ttm_device.c:69-126) with no arguments. It takes ttm_global_mutex and increments ttm_glob_use_count; if the count is then above 1 it releases the mutex and returns 0 without initialising anything. Otherwise it creates the debugfs directory (an error leaves the root NULL), computes the pool page limits from system memory, initialises the pool and TT managers, allocates the dummy read page (with GFP_DMA32, retrying without it and logging a warning), initialises the device list and the buffer-object counter and creates the buffer_objects debugfs file. If both page allocations fail it sets -ENOMEM, removes the debugfs root, decrements the use count and returns -ENOMEM; the pool and TT managers initialised earlier are not torn down here. The mutex is released on every path. On success (including the early-success path) the caller holds a use-count reference that must be released later (ttm_global_release).
note: Checked against ttm_device.c:69-126. Reviewer claims: omits the early success path when the use count was already above 1 (right, 77-78), the success path takes a reference by incrementing the use count (right), and the old contract omitted these side effects (right); the old contract is left empty. R:right

name: vbox_crtc_set_base_and_mode
prose: Static void (vbox_mode.c:177-218). Before taking the lock it reads fb->obj[0] as a GEM VRAM object and evaluates drm_atomic_crtc_needs_modeset(crtc->state). It then takes vbox->hw_mutex and, if crtc->state->enable is set, copies the mode's hdisplay and vdisplay into vbox_crtc->width and height; it always stores x, y and the VRAM offset of the framebuffer's object. Only when a modeset is needed and vbox_set_up_input_mapping returns true does it call vbox_do_modeset on every other CRTC. It then always calls vbox_set_view and vbox_do_modeset for this CRTC and, when a modeset is needed, sends the current input mapping size to the host with hgsmi_update_input_mapping. It releases the mutex and returns nothing.
note: Checked against vbox_mode.c:177-218. Reviewer claims: other CRTCs are redone only when vbox_set_up_input_mapping returns true (right, 198), vbox_set_up_input_mapping is only called when needs_modeset (right, 198), and crtc->state is read before the mutex is taken (right, 181-184). R:right

name: vc4_submit_cl_ioctl
prose: Returns int (vc4_gem.c:1016-1163). It returns -ENODEV if the VC4 generation is above 4 or no V3D is probed, -EINVAL for unknown flag bits or a nonzero pad2, and -ENOMEM if the exec allocation fails. It then takes a V3D runtime-PM reference with vc4_v3d_pm_get; on failure it frees the exec with kfree and returns the error directly. Afterwards errors go to cleanup through vc4_complete_exec (and drm_exec_fini when the BO reservations were taken): the lookup of the BOs, -ENOENT for an unknown perfmon id, drm_syncobj_find_fence and dma_fence_wait for the in fence (the wait is skipped for fences of this context), vc4_get_bcl, vc4_get_rcl, vc4_lock_bo_reservations, -EINVAL for an out_sync that does not resolve to a syncobj, and vc4_queue_submit. The out_sync reference is dropped after the queue attempt whether or not it succeeded. On success it stores vc4->emit_seqno in args->seqno and returns 0; the exec, the runtime-PM reference and the BO references now belong to the queued job and are released when the job completes, not by this function.
note: Checked against vc4_gem.c:1016-1163. Reviewer claim (a pm_get failure frees the exec with kfree and returns directly, not through drm_exec_fini and vc4_complete_exec) is right (1060-1064). The old prose also claimed the runtime-PM reference and exec are released on success, which is wrong: the exec is owned by the queued job. R:right

name: vmw_context_init
prose: Static int (vmwgfx_context.c:241-291). If dev_priv->has_mob is set it returns the result of vmw_gb_context_init(dev_priv, dx, res, res_free) unchanged. Otherwise it calls vmw_resource_init with the legacy context functions; if that fails it logs, frees res with res_free (or kfree when res_free is NULL) and returns the error. It returns -ENOMEM after unreferencing res when res->id is at least SVGA3D_HB_MAX_CONTEXT_IDS or when VMW_CMD_RESERVE fails. On success it fills and commits an SVGA_3D_CMD_CONTEXT_DEFINE command for res->id, calls vmw_fifo_resource_inc, sets res->hw_destroy to vmw_hw_context_destroy and returns 0.

name: vmw_present_readback_ioctl
prose: Returns int (vmwgfx_ioctl.c:248-318). It returns 0 at once when arg->num_clips is 0. It returns -EINVAL when clips_ptr is NULL, -ENOMEM if the clip array allocation fails, -EFAULT if the copy from user space fails. It then takes the modeset lock (drm_modeset_lock_all), looks the framebuffer up by id (-ENOENT if missing), returns -EINVAL if the framebuffer is not buffer backed, and otherwise returns the result of vmw_kms_readback. On every path after the lock the framebuffer reference (when taken) is dropped, the modeset lock is released and the clip array is freed.

name: vmw_surface_tex_dirty_range_add
prose: Static void (vmwgfx_surface.c:1845-1890). It clamps start to the resource's guest memory offset and end to the guest memory end, makes both relative to that offset, finds the surface locations of the first byte and of the position just after the last byte, and updates the dirty tracker in dirty->cache. If the two locations are on different multisample sheets it marks every subresource fully dirty and returns. If the range lies in a single subresource (the end location is the next subresource) it adds the range with vmw_subres_dirty_add; otherwise it adds the part of the first subresource from the start location to its end, the part of the last subresource from its start to the end location, and marks the subresources in between fully dirty. The range must be non-empty (end - 1 is used), and the function returns nothing.
note: Checked against vmwgfx_surface.c:1845-1890. Reviewer claim (the function clamps start and end itself) is right. R:right

name: vmw_surface_buf_dirty_range_add
prose: Static void (vmwgfx_surface.c:1896-1914). It sets boxes[0].h and boxes[0].d to 1, clamps start to the resource's guest memory offset and end to the offset plus cache->mip_chain_bytes (both made relative to the offset), and updates box x and width: if the box is empty or its x is above start it sets x to start, and if the box's old right edge is below end it sets the width to end minus box x; boxes[0].y and z are not changed. For in-order additions this gives the union of the old box and the range, but when the range is below the old right edge and the old box x is moved down the width is left unchanged, so an out-of-order range can shrink the box on the right and lose previously recorded bytes. It returns nothing.
note: Checked against vmwgfx_surface.c:1896-1914. Reviewer claim (the code clamps start and end itself, and the union logic can shrink the box for out-of-order ranges) is right (1907-1913). R:right

name: vmw_dumb_create
prose: Returns int (vmwgfx_surface.c:2247-2364) and creates a dumb buffer. It chooses a surface format from the bpp. If the device has no MOB support or no 3D support it computes cpp from the bpp and returns -EINVAL unless cpp is 1, 2 or 4, sets args->pitch and args->size (page aligned), creates a GEM object with a handle via vmw_gem_object_create_with_handle, drops the extra GEM reference and returns that result. Otherwise it builds a guest-backed surface request (scanout, shareable, coherent, buffer-creating) and calls vmw_gb_surface_define_ext_ioctl; on failure it logs and returns the error with nothing created. On success it sets args->handle and args->size from the reply and args->pitch from the surface description, then looks up the surface by the reply handle; if that fails it logs and goes to err, which unreferences res (if set) and drops the tfile handle reference and returns the error. If it succeeds it marks the buffer object as dumb with the surface, drops the GEM reference, clears the user surface's refcount_release callback, and at err releases the resource reference and the tfile handle reference and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: the function is vmw_dumb_create (head at vmwgfx_surface.c:2247), not vmw_dumb_create_internal. The old prose omitted the non-MOB path (-EINVAL for unsupported cpp). R:n/a

name: xe_exec_ioctl
prose: Returns int (xe_exec.c:110-379) and submits a batch (or just syncs) on an exec queue. It returns -EINVAL for extensions, nonzero padding or reserved fields or more than DRM_XE_MAX_SYNCS syncs, and -ENOENT when the exec queue is not found. After that every error goes through cleanup labels that drop the queue reference: -EINVAL for a VM-bind queue or a batch-buffer count that does not match the queue width, -ECANCELED when the queue's reset status is set, -ENOMEM if the sync array allocation fails, errors from xe_sync_entry_parse, -EINVAL if more than one user fence is given, -EFAULT if the batch addresses cannot be copied. For the DMA-fence engine-group mode it gets the engine group mode (error returned). It takes the VM lock for writing (and repins userptrs) when a userptr repin is needed, otherwise for reading (interruptible); when the call has no batch buffers it takes the VM lock object, signals the syncs with a fence from the input syncs and finishes (returning 0 through the unlock path without creating a job). Otherwise it waits for pm_block, locks the VM objects and validates (non-LR VMs), returns -ECANCELED when the VM is closed or banned, returns -EWOULDBLOCK (with skip_retry set) when an LR queue's ring is full, validates PXP-protected VMs, creates the job, adds dependencies from the VM objects and syncs, takes the notifier lock and checks whether a userptr repin is needed, then arms the job, adds fences, signals syncs, pushes the job and reactivates rebinds. If the last step set err to -EAGAIN (and skip_retry is false) it retries from the VM lock. On success err is 0. All paths release the VM lock, the validation context, the job reference on failure, the engine group reference, the syncs and the queue reference.
note: slice cut the head: the function is xe_exec_ioctl (head at xe_exec.c:110); the old item name xe_exec_queue_submit_job_path does not exist. Old prose assumed the VM lock is held by the caller; this function takes it. R:n/a

name: xe_gt_sriov_pf_config_set_dbs
prose: Returns int (xe_gt_sriov_pf_config.c:1179-1196) and sets the doorbell quota of a function (vfid 0 is the PF's spare) under the PF master mutex, which it takes and releases itself. For vfid 0 it calls pf_set_spare_dbs, which returns -EINVAL when num_dbs exceeds GUC_NUM_DOORBELLS or when it is nonzero and below the minimum spare, otherwise stores the spare. For a VF it calls pf_provision_vf_dbs, which returns -EINVAL when num_dbs exceeds GUC_NUM_DOORBELLS, and, if the VF already has doorbells, first pushes a zero configuration to the GuC (failure returns that error with the old quota unchanged), then releases the old doorbells and refreshes the configuration (a failure here leaves the quota at 0); with num_dbs 0 it then returns 0; otherwise it reserves doorbells (error returned, quota 0), stores them and pushes the configuration (a push failure releases them again, quota 0), returning 0 on success with the quota equal to num_dbs. The final return value is the error of that step, or 0, via pf_config_set_u32_done, which only logs the result (it does not compare the requested and actual values, so no -EINVAL for a mismatch).
note: Checked against xe_gt_sriov_pf_config.c:1179-1196, 1092-1131, 1051-1064 and 875-894. Reviewer claims: a failure after releasing the old config leaves the quota at zero, not unchanged (right, 1107-1111 and 1126); -EINVAL for vfid 0 with num_dbs above the maximum (right, 1056); round 15 claim (pf_config_set_u32_done returns -EINVAL when requested differs from actual) is wrong: it returns err or 0. R:mixed

name: vf_query_runtime_info
prose: Static int (xe_gt_sriov_vf.c:832-909). It returns -ENOPKG at once (before touching the runtime table) if the negotiated PF interface version is below 1.0. Otherwise it sends VF2PF_QUERY_RUNTIME requests through the GuC relay, starting at 0 and asking for up to 16 registers per response. A negative result of the send, a response shorter than the minimum length, a payload of odd size, or a count field different from the number of entries goes to failed with -EPROTO (or the send error). On the first response (start 0) it calls vf_prepare_runtime_info for num + remaining entries (a failure goes to failed); on later responses it returns -EPROTO via failed if start + num exceeds the recorded size. It copies the reported offset and value pairs into gt->sriov.vf.runtime.regs and repeats with start advanced while remaining is nonzero. When remaining is 0 it returns 0 without checking that the table was completely filled. At failed it calls vf_prepare_runtime_info(gt, 0), which resets the runtime table, and returns the error.
note: Checked against xe_gt_sriov_vf.c:832-909. Reviewer claims: the -ENOPKG path returns before the table is reset (right, 845-846), success returns 0 without verifying the table is completely filled (right, 899-904), the cleanup call vf_prepare_runtime_info(gt, 0) resets the existing table (right, 906-908). R:right

name: __guc_ct_send_locked
prose: Static int (xe_guc_ct.c:870-941); the caller holds ct->lock. It returns -EPIPE if the H2G buffer is marked broken, -ENODEV if the CT state is disabled, -ECANCELED if it is stopped (all through the out label, before any other lock is taken). With a g2h_fence it uses the maximum G2H length and one expected G2H, and if the fence needs a sequence number it assigns one and stores the fence in ct->fence_lookup with xa_store (a failure returns its xa_err result with seqno already assigned but the fence not registered); without a fence it takes the next ordinary sequence number. It takes ct->fast_lock (spin_lock_irq) only when g2h_len is nonzero, and releases it on every path after that. It then loops: has_room (nonzero result, which is -EPIPE for a broken buffer or -EBUSY for lack of H2G or G2H space, goes to out_unlock), then h2g_write: -EAGAIN (a ring wrap) retries from has_room (with fast_lock held only if g2h_len is nonzero), another nonzero result goes to out_unlock. On success it reserves g2h_len dwords of G2H space and num_g2h replies, notifies the GuC and returns 0.
note: Checked against xe_guc_ct.c:870-941. Reviewer claims: fast_lock is only taken when g2h_len is nonzero (right, 920-921 and 937-938); h2g_write can also return -EPIPE for a corrupted buffer and the lock is released then (right); the -EAGAIN retry may run without fast_lock when g2h_len is zero (right). R:right

name: guc_exec_queue_timedout_job
prose: Static enum drm_gpu_sched_stat (xe_guc_submit.c:1226-1438), the DRM scheduler timeout handler of a GuC exec queue. It returns DRM_GPU_SCHED_STAT_NO_HANG at once, before stopping submission, if the job's fence is already signalled. Otherwise it stops scheduler submission, decides whether to skip the timeout check (reset, killed, banned, wedged or destroyed queue), optionally captures a snapshot under forcewake (releasing it before continuing), and determines whether the device is wedged. For a registered queue while not wedged it may wait up to 5 s for pending enable and disable, disable scheduling and wait again; if a wait fails or the GuC reading is stopped it takes the trigger_reset path: devcoredump, sets an extra queue reference (taken for the asynchronous GT reset), bans the queue, starts an async GT reset, queues an immediate TDR and goes to rearm. If the job is not actually timed out (not wedged, timeout check not skipped, no reset, still registered) it clears the check flag and goes to sched_enable, which re-enables scheduling and then to rearm. For a kernel or VM queue (not wedged) it tries to invalidate the job: if that fails it clears the check flag, starts an async GT reset (without banning the queue or taking an extra reference) and goes to rearm. Otherwise it bans the queue; for a registered, not destroyed queue (not wedged) it takes an extra reference and deregisters it. It then stops the fence irq, re-adds the job to the pending list, restarts submission, triggers queue cleanup, sets the error of the pending jobs (the first gets err, the rest -ECANCELED), restarts the fence irq and returns DRM_GPU_SCHED_STAT_RESET. At rearm it restarts submission and returns DRM_GPU_SCHED_STAT_NO_HANG.
note: slice cut the head: the function is guc_exec_queue_timedout_job (head at xe_guc_submit.c:1226; the slice started at 1270). Reviewer claim (the kernel/VM invalidation path does not ban the queue or take an extra reference before the async GT reset) is right (1388-1394). The old prose also said submission is always restarted; the first early return skips both stop and restart. R:right

name: pf_disable_vfs
prose: Static int (xe_pci_sriov.c:205-230). It reads the number of enabled VFs from PCI, asserts that the device is a PF, logs a debug message (before the zero check), and returns 0 at once with no other effect when no VF is enabled. Otherwise it disables engine activity statistics for the VFs, calls pci_disable_sriov, resets each VF with pf_reset_vfs, unprovisions the VFs on every GT with pf_unprovision_vfs, releases the runtime-PM reference taken when the VFs were enabled with xe_pm_runtime_put, logs an info message and returns 0. It always returns 0.
note: Checked against xe_pci_sriov.c:205-230. Reviewer claims: the formal contract omitted the side effects (right), and the debug log is emitted before the zero check so the zero-VF path is not entirely free of effects (right, 212). R:right

name: xe_pcode_request
prose: Returns int (xe_pcode.c:181-216). It asserts timeout_base_ms is at most 3, takes tile->pcode.lock and calls pcode_try_request with timeout_base_ms * 1000 microseconds without disabling preemption; if that returns 0 it unlocks and returns. Otherwise it logs, disables preemption and retries for 50 ms with atomic delays. pcode_try_request polls the mailbox with exponentially growing waits and returns 0 as soon as the mailbox status is 0 and (request & reply_mask) == reply; it returns -ETIMEDOUT otherwise. The status of each mailbox transaction (0, -EAGAIN when the mailbox was busy before the request, the wait-for-ready error (-ETIMEDOUT) or one of the PCODE error codes) is stored in status. The function returns the last status if nonzero, else the pcode_try_request result. With skip_pcode set the mailbox status is 0, so it returns 0 only if request already satisfies the reply mask, else -ETIMEDOUT. The request value is passed by value and is not modified; no reply is returned.
note: Checked against xe_pcode.c:33-86, 134-160 and 181-216. Reviewer claims: -EAGAIN is possible (right), skip_pcode does not guarantee 0 (right), request is not overwritten (right), and the wait-for-ready timeout is -ETIMEDOUT rather than -EAGAIN (right, 75-78). R:right
